geometry.position: The top-left corner in logical display pixels. Inside a container this is measured from the container box rather than from the screen.
geometry.size: Width and height in logical display pixels.
geometry.z: Drawing order among siblings: a higher value is drawn later, so it covers a lower one. Widgets with the same value keep the order of the layer list.

data.binding: The telemetry field this widget reads. Names come from the catalog, so the device binds them once at startup and never looks one up while drawing.
data.modifier: A stateful reading of the field, computed on the device. The lap timer turns the current lap time into one that keeps running between the updates SimHub sends.
data.range: The window the value is read against: the widget shows where the value sits between the two, clamped at both ends. The unit is the one the bound field reports.

text.sources: Sources are rendered in order, each through its own transform, into one string. The prefix and suffix are what separate one from the next, so "P 3/24" is a position source followed by a participants source prefixed with "/".
text.transform: How the raw value becomes text. A number is scaled, offset and rounded; a duration is formatted as a lap time. Only the transforms the bound field supports are offered.
text.preset: A ready scale, offset and suffix for the usual unit conversions of this field — kph to mph, celsius to fahrenheit.
text.scale: Applied before the offset: the drawn number is value × scale + offset, rounded to the decimals set beside it.
text.affix: Literal text drawn immediately before and after this source. With several sources this is the only separator between them.
text.alignment: Where the text sits inside the widget box, after the padding is taken off.
text.fallback: Drawn while the field has no value yet — before the first telemetry frame arrives, or when the game does not report it. Empty draws nothing.

title.fallback: A second installed family to try for glyphs the first does not have — an icon family beside a text one, which is how a value carries an icon and its number in one widget. It is built at the same size, so it costs one more font.
title.text: A caption drawn on the widget box. Clearing the text removes the caption entirely, which is what a panel used as a container or a tap zone usually wants.
title.source: Telemetry the caption reads instead of the text, so a label can name what the widget is showing. The text stays the fallback: it is what the caption reads until the field arrives, and what the widget box is sized against.
title.font: The family comes from the font library and the size is this caption’s alone — the board holds one face per family and rasterizes any size from it.
title.alignment: The point on the widget box the caption is anchored to. The top and bottom rows straddle their border line; the middle row sits inside the box.
title.offset: Moves the caption from its anchor, in pixels. Positive is right and down.
title.cut: A caption on the top or bottom row breaks the border line it sits on instead of being drawn over it. Turn this off to draw the border straight through.
title.gap: How much clear space the cut leaves on each side of the caption.

box.fillCorners: How the background and a value fill meet the rounded corners. Rounded gives them the same curve; square leaves them straight and cuts them on the box outline instead, so a bar keeps a flat leading edge while its ends still follow the rounding.
box.background: The fill behind the widget. Unset draws nothing, which is what leaves the screen background showing through.
box.gradient: The far end of the background fill. On the ESP32-P4 a gradient falls back to the software renderer, which costs frame time.
box.axis: The direction the background gradient runs in.
box.padding: Keeps the contents this far inside the box on each side. It does not move the box itself.
box.border: The outline drawn on the box edge. A zero width draws none.
box.radius: Rounds the box corners, border and background alike.
box.inset: Shrinks the background fill inside the border by this much, so a thick border and its fill do not overlap on the curve.

conditions.source: The field the rules are read against. It is independent of what the widget shows, so a gear readout can turn red on engine speed.
conditions.ramp: Moves the colour smoothly with the value between the stops. Rules paint over it; a ramp alone needs at least two stops.
conditions.rampTarget: Which part of the widget the ramp colours.
conditions.rule: The first rule that holds wins. Anything a rule leaves unset stays as authored, so a rule may change only the colour and nothing else.
conditions.blink: Alternates the widget on and off while the rule holds. Zero leaves it steady.
conditions.hold: Keeps the rule applied for this long after it stops holding, so a momentary event stays readable. Zero applies it only while it holds.

action.tap: What a tap on this widget does on a board with a digitizer. An empty transparent shape with an action is an invisible tap zone.
action.screen: The screen a tap goes to, named rather than numbered — renaming a screen repoints every action that names it.

container.clip: Whether the contents end at this box. With it off, a widget inside is drawn where it lands even past the box, which is what a caption straddling a child’s top border needs.

ring.centreAngle: The middle of the sector. Zero degrees is three o’clock and the angle grows clockwise, so 270 points straight up and a 270 sector around it is the usual car gauge.
ring.sector: How wide the sector is. Half of it falls either side of the centre angle.
ring.thickness: How thick the band is. It grows either side of the radius, so the radius stays where it is.
ring.radius: Radius of the band’s centre line. Zero takes it from the box, which is what an arc has always done. A radius of its own may be larger than the box: the widget still clips to its box, so only the band crossing it is drawn.
ring.centering: What the box centres. circle puts the middle of the ring’s circle in the middle of the box. figure centres what is drawn — the band between the sector’s ends, thickness included — so raising the radius keeps the band in the middle of the box and pushes the circle’s centre out of it instead.
ring.offset: Moves the circle away from the centre of the box and never changes its radius. Pushing it outside the box, with a radius to match, is how a shallow band across the top of a round display is authored.

arc.track: The unfilled part of the arc. Unset leaves it undrawn.
arc.mark: What the value draws at its angle. A ring fills the sector up to it; a needle points a line from the centre at it, as thick as the ring would be, with the track left as the scale behind it.
arc.inverted: Fills from the far end of the sector instead of the near one.

bar.origin: The fill runs between this value and the current one instead of from the minimum, so a signed window with a zero origin reads as a centred meter.
bar.fill: The colour of the filled part. The box background underneath is the track the fill runs over.
bar.inverted: Fills from the far end of the bar instead of from the near one.

strip.segments: Each lamp lights at its own fraction of the range, so one strip suits any engine. Thresholds must not decrease down the list.
strip.gap: The space left between lamps, and the corner radius of each one. An arc spends the gap along its own ring, and any non-zero radius rounds the lamp ends instead.
strip.shape: A strip runs the lamps along its orientation. An arc spaces them around a sector, which is the rev ring a round dashboard is built on.
strip.blink: Blinking starts at this fraction of the range. A threshold above 1 never blinks, and neither does a zero period.
strip.off: The colour of a lamp that is not lit. Unset leaves it undrawn.
strip.inverted: Lights from the far end instead of the near one, which is what makes a mirrored pair of rev bars out of one authored strip. Which lamp lights when does not change.

graph.points: How many samples each trace keeps and how often one is taken — together they are the window the plot shows. One clock for the whole widget, so several traces line up along it. The trace is the most expensive widget to draw, so keep the point count only as high as it needs to be.
graph.traces: Further sources drawn over the same plot, up to three in all counting the widget’s own. Each carries its own range, which is what lets speed and throttle share one field without either flattening against an edge.
graph.width: Thickness of every trace. Half of it is kept clear inside the plot on each side — plus whatever a rounded frame needs for the corners to clear the curve — so a value at the top or the bottom of its range is drawn whole rather than cut by the frame.

image.image: Images are uploaded to the board and converted in the configurator to the size they are drawn at. The device neither scales nor rotates, so match the widget box to the bitmap.
image.frame: Which picture of a sprite sheet to draw. A sheet is several images uploaded as one, so switching between them costs nothing on the board and spends one of its 32 entries rather than one per picture.
image.frameSource: Chooses the picture from telemetry instead: the value is rounded to a whole number and clamped to the frames the sheet holds, so 0 is the first and anything past the last stays on the last. This is what draws a gear, a flag or a lamp set from one widget rather than a stack of them.
image.recolor: Tints the bitmap towards this colour, which is how one white icon serves every state. An alpha8 image is the colour rather than tinted by it: it carries only coverage, and is drawn white until this says otherwise.
image.strength: How far the tint goes, from untouched at 0 to fully the tint colour at 255. An alpha8 image ignores it — there the colour is the image, not a tint over one.

shape.kind: A line is a thin rectangle: give it a small height or width. A shape is also the container other widgets are placed inside.

slot.pages: A tap on the board cycles the pages that are in the loop. Page order is priority: when two are triggered at once the device shows the earlier one.
slot.loop: Whether a tap on the slot can reach this page. A page out of the loop is only ever raised by its trigger.
slot.trigger: What raises this page over the loop on its own. Without one the page is reached only by tapping the slot.
slot.duration: How long the page stays up. A value-changed trigger needs one; with rules, zero shows the page only while a rule holds.

dashboard.transition: How the board swaps one screen for another, whether a swipe or a tap asked for it. slide is the sliding animation; none replaces the screen in a single frame. The slide draws both screens for every one of its frames, so a screen full of widgets is where it is felt — set this to none if swiping stutters.
dashboard.smoothing: Whether bars, arcs, needles, graph traces and number-formatted text move between telemetry packets instead of stepping with them. interpolate glides to each packet so as to arrive when the next is due: perfectly smooth, one packet period behind (16 ms at 60 Hz, 50 ms at 20 Hz). predict keeps moving at the measured rate and corrects when the packet lands: nothing behind on average, a small overshoot on reversals. A pause longer than 250 ms between packets is drawn as a jump, so values that change on events never glide. Indicators, conditions and captions always read the packet itself.
dashboard.font: The family new widgets take. It is the editor’s own setting — the device resolves a font per widget, so the document carries no dashboard-wide one.
dashboard.budget: What the chosen families cost on the board. Faces are uploaded whole and the partition holds 2 MiB of them.

screen.name: What a "go to screen" action points at. Renaming repoints every action that names this screen.
screen.background: The colour behind every widget on this screen.

widget.id: The name this widget is known by in the layer list, in the JSON, and to anything that refers to it. The device stores it and never draws it.

conditionsEditor.holdInMillisecondsAfterThe: Hold in milliseconds after the rule stops holding
conditionsEditor.aRampNeedsAtLeast: A ramp needs at least two stops to interpolate between.

iconPicker.anIconIsAGlyph: An icon is a glyph of the Material Icons family — set that family on the text it lands in.

stylingEditors.title: Title
stylingEditors.theCutIsAStraight: The cut is a straight band, so a caption pushed into a rounded corner takes a bite out of it. Offset it by about the radius plus the border width to clear the curve.

widgetEditors.uploadImagesToTheBoard: Upload images to the board to choose one here.
widgetEditors.theSlotDrawsNothingItself: The slot draws nothing itself — put a shape behind it for a background. Every page is this box, and its widgets are placed relative to it.
widgetEditors.imageIsNotInstalledOn: "{image}" is not installed on the connected board, so the device will refuse this configuration.
widgetEditors.imageHasASingleFrame: "{image}" has a single frame, so the device will refuse a frame or a frame source on it.
widgetEditors.thisShapeHoldsNoWidgets: This shape holds no widgets. Select some and wrap them to make it a container; an empty one with an action is an invisible tap zone.
widgetEditors.holdsHeldWidgetSPlaced: Holds {held} widget(s), placed relative to this box.

propertyRow.labelIsSetInThis: {label} is set in this document — click to clear it

output.pin: GPIO the chain’s data line is wired to. Only pins the board leaves free are offered — the display, the flash, the PSRAM, the serial link and the status lamp own the rest, and the firmware refuses any of them.
output.chip: Which family the lamps are. ws2812b also covers WS2812, WS2813 and WS2815: they read the same three bytes and differ only in supply and redundancy. sk6812_rgbw has a fourth, white lamp in each package, so a neutral colour moves onto it and the chain takes a third longer to clock out.
output.brightness: Scales every colour on this output on its way to the wire, before the current limit. It is the one brightness the device has — layers carry none of their own.
output.gamma: Corrects the perceptual response of the lamps. Without it the bottom of the brightness range is a handful of visibly separate steps rather than a fade.
output.current: Ceiling on what this output may draw. The whole frame is scaled down when the estimate passes it, so the picture dims evenly rather than the supply sagging and the colours drifting. A lamp at full white draws around 60 mA, so one eight-by-eight panel is already past what a USB port can give. Leave it at 0 only if you know the supply.

device.count: Lamps in this strip. With an arrangement described below, it is the sum of the runs.
device.segments: How the strip is physically mounted, as straight runs in wire order — say 8 lamps up the left side, 16 across the top, 8 down the right. The board clocks the chain out the same either way; the runs bend the previews to match the mounting and give profiles ready-made targets. Their counts must add up to the whole strip.
device.size: Columns and rows of the panel, as it is built rather than as it is mounted.
device.wiring: How the panel is wired and how it is mounted. Rows says whether alternate rows run backwards, which most ready-made panels do. First lamp names the corner the data line enters. Turn rotates everything drawn on the panel, so one mounted on its side still reads upright.

sprite.pictures: Pictures this panel can draw, each a grid of palette-indexed pixels and up to sixteen frames of it. They travel inside the modules document rather than being uploaded, so they cost no partition, no upload and no restart — and a saved configuration carries its own artwork.
sprite.name: What layers name this picture by. Renaming it follows through to every layer that draws it. Two pictures on one panel may not share a name.
sprite.size: Columns and rows of the picture itself, which need not match the panel: a smaller picture is drawn centred on whatever the layer paints on. The bigger it is the fewer frames fit, because every picture shares the same 1024-digit budget.
sprite.palette: Colours this picture is drawn from, at most fifteen of them. Pick one to paint with, or Clear to leave a pixel unpainted so the layers below stay visible — that is a digit past the end of the palette rather than a colour, which is why the last one is kept free. Entry 1 is the unlit lamp by convention rather than by rule: it paints black over whatever is under it.
sprite.frames: Frames of the animation, played in order by a layer with Play frames switched on. How many fit follows the size: sixteen of eight by eight, four of sixteen by sixteen. Duplicate a frame to draw the next one from it.
sprite.mirror: Plays this picture on the connected board while you draw, on its own, the way a layer previews. Needs a board and live apply switched on; the panel goes back to the whole configuration when it is switched off.

effect.stack: Every layer whose gate holds paints at once. Where two of them cover the same lamp, the one that lit most recently wins it — so a flag comes up over shift lights whichever way round the two are listed — and layers that came up together keep the order they are in here. This is the opposite of a widget’s styling rules, where the first match wins: a widget resolves one appearance, while an output composes a picture out of many things being true at once.
effect.type: What this layer paints. steps is the shift-light idiom: thresholds shared out over the lamps it covers. gauge fills in proportion to the value. gradient spreads a colour ramp across the lamps. animation moves on its own timebase. sprite and text draw on a matrix.
effect.area: Which run of this device’s lamps the layer paints. Lamps are numbered from 1 here, while the saved document counts them from zero. A count of 0 covers the rest of the device.
effect.panel: Which pixels of the panel this layer paints on. Click one to turn it off or on, or drag across several; All and Invert do the whole grid at once. Every pixel is the default and costs the document nothing. The layer works over the smallest box holding what you picked, so text and a picture still centre on the shape rather than on the panel.
effect.sprite: Which of the panel’s pictures this layer draws. Pictures are drawn on the Pictures tab, and a profile brings its own — the flags carry their artwork with them; a layer whose picture the panel does not carry is a composition error rather than a blank panel.
effect.loop: Walks the picture’s frames on this layer’s own clock, one every frame time, which is how artwork moves without telemetry driving it. Left off, the layer holds the one frame named below.
effect.gate: When this layer paints at all. always paints on every frame; conditions paints while a rule over its own watched value holds; telemetry idle paints only after two seconds of silence, which is what an idle animation and a lost-link warning both want.
effect.hold: Keeps the layer painting for this long after its gate stops holding, so a momentary event such as traction control still produces a visible flash.
effect.background: Fills every lamp this layer covers before it draws, so a glyph or a picture sits on a ground of its own rather than on whatever the layers below left. Off paints no ground, which is what a layer over shift lights wants.
effect.ruleTiming: Blink is the period the whole layer flashes at while this rule holds, so one band of a value can flash without a second layer over it; it takes over from the layer’s own blink. Hold keeps the rule applied for that long after it stops matching, so a momentary trigger still leaves a visible flash of colour.
effect.colors: Colours this layer takes while the watched value matches, the first matching rule winning — a gear that turns amber and then red as the revs climb. They describe rather than select: the gate says whether the layer paints at all, these say what colour it paints in. On a picture the colour repaints every lit pixel, so one drawing serves every state — the pixels it paints black stay black.
effect.blink: Full blink period of everything this layer paints. 0 paints steady.
effect.shape: Which way the layer fills the lamps it covers. Along the run starts at the first lamp; backwards starts at the last. Out from the middle paints both ways at once from the centre, which is what a centred rev bar wants; in from the ends does the opposite, closing on the centre.

toolPalette.theDashboardAlreadyHoldsAs: The dashboard already holds as many {toLowerCase} widgets as the board has room for.

fonts.everyDashboardFontMustExplicitly: Every dashboard font must explicitly define a valid family and size_px.
fonts.configurationReferencesMoreThanMaximum: Configuration references more than {mAXIMUM_FONT_FAMILIES} font families.

hardware.labelIsAMatrixWhose: {label} is a matrix, whose arrangement is its grid rather than a list of runs.
hardware.labelArrangesArrangedLampsOver: {label} arranges {arranged} lamps over its runs, but the strip drives {lamps}.
hardware.labelIsAStripSo: {label} is a strip, so it has nothing to draw a sprite on.
hardware.labelCarriesASpriteWith: {label} carries a sprite with no id.
hardware.ownerCarriesLengthPixelDigits: {owner} carries {length} pixel digits; its geometry needs {expected}.
hardware.ownerCarriesDigitWhichIs: {owner} carries {digit}, which is not a hexadecimal pixel digit.
hardware.theHardwareSectionMustBe: The hardware section must be a list of peripherals.
hardware.theConfigurationDeclaresLengthDevices: The configuration declares {length} devices; this board drives at most {outputs}, one transmit channel each.
hardware.labelNamesNoTypeSo: {label} names no "type", so nothing says which peripheral it is.
hardware.labelIsATypePeripheral: {label} is a {type} peripheral, which this firmware has no driver for.
hardware.twoDevicesAreWiredTo: Two devices are wired to pin {pin}.
hardware.labelIsRotatedByRotation: {label} is rotated by {rotation_deg}°; only 0, 90, 180 and 270 are quarter turns.
hardware.labelDrivesLampsLampsOne: {label} drives {lamps} lamps; one device carries at most {mAXIMUM_LEDS_PER_OUTPUT}.
hardware.theConfigurationDrivesTotalLamps: The configuration drives {total} lamps; a board carries at most {mAXIMUM_LEDS_TOTAL}.
hardware.labelNamesPinPinBut: {label} names pin {pin}, but this board publishes no free pins for LEDs yet.

ledValues.labelMustCarryItsWhat: {label} must carry its {what} as a list.
ledValues.labelDrawsASpriteNamed: {label} draws a sprite named {sprite}, which this device does not carry.
ledValues.labelNamesFrameSpriteFrame: {label} names frame {sprite_frame}, but the sprite holds {frames}.
ledValues.labelNamesPanelPixelsWhich: {label} names panel pixels, which only a matrix has.
ledValues.labelCarriesLengthMaskDigits: {label} carries {length} mask digits; a {width} by {height} panel needs {expected}.
ledValues.labelCarriesDigitInIts: {label} carries {digit} in its mask, which is not a hexadecimal digit.
ledValues.labelMustCarryItsSource: {label} must carry its source modifiers as a list.
ledValues.labelCarriesASourceModifier: {label} carries a source modifier, which an LED layer cannot apply.
ledValues.labelIsATypeLayer: {label} is a {type} layer, which needs a matrix rather than a strip.
ledValues.labelIsATypeLayer2: {label} is a {type} layer and reads no telemetry, so its source would sit unread.
ledValues.labelIsATypeLayer3: {label} is a {type} layer and needs telemetry to map.
ledValues.labelNeedsAWatchedSource: {label} needs a watched source for its gate and its colour rules, and none without them.
ledValues.labelCarriesStrayAmongIts: {label} carries {stray} among its {what}, which is not one.
ledValues.labelSetsKeyToSomething: {label} sets "{key}" to something that is not a number.
ledValues.labelIsAGradientWhich: {label} is a gradient, which needs at least two colour stops.
ledValues.labelIsAStepsLayer: {label} is a steps layer, which needs at least one step.
ledValues.labelIsAGaugeWith: {label} is a gauge with a single colour stop; give it none, or two or more.
ledValues.labelIsATextLayer: {label} is a text layer with neither text nor a source to render.

ranges.ownerSetsKeyToSomething: {owner} sets "{key}" to something that is not a number.

schemaKeys.unknownPropertyHereIsNot: Unknown property "{here}" is not part of the configuration schema.
schemaKeys.pathMustBeAnArray: "{path}" must be an array of widgets.

structure.dashboardScreensMustBeAn: "dashboard.screens" must be an array of screens.
structure.aDashboardCarriesAtMost: A dashboard carries at most {mAXIMUM_SCREENS} screen(s); this one declares {length}.
structure.thisBoardHasNoDisplay: This board has no display, so the dashboard cannot declare screens.
structure.labelIsASlotInside: {label} is a slot inside a container; a slot sits directly on a screen.
structure.thisDashboardUsesCountType: This dashboard uses {count} {type} widgets; the device stores {cap}.
structure.thisDashboardHasActionsTap: This dashboard has {actions} tap targets; the device binds at most {mAXIMUM_ACTIONS}.
structure.thisDashboardHasLaptimersSources: This dashboard has {lapTimers} sources using the lap timer; the device runs one.

transforms.whatOfLabelIsA: {what} of {label} is a time transform with no format; the device needs "duration_ms", "clock_ms" or "signed_duration_ms".
transforms.whatOfLabelTimesBinding: {what} of {label} times "{binding}", which the device carries as {type}; a {_ms} is {counted} whole number of milliseconds.
transforms.whatOfLabelPutsA: {what} of {label} puts a number transform on "{binding}", which is true or false and has nothing to scale.
transforms.whatOfLabelAsksFor: {what} of {label} asks for {decimals} decimals; the device writes at most {mAXIMUM_TRANSFORM_DECIMALS}.
transforms.whatOfLabelScalesBinding: {what} of {label} scales "{binding}" by something that is not a finite number.

transport.thisBoardHasNoNative: This board has no native USB port; telemetry has to run over its UART.
transport.thisBoardHasNoUart: This board has no UART for telemetry; it talks over its native USB port.
transport.theUartRunsAtBaudrate: The UART runs at {baudRate} bits per second; the device accepts {mINIMUM_BAUD_RATE} to {mAXIMUM_BAUD_RATE}.

widgetGeometry.labelPadsFurtherThanThe: {label} pads further than the display is wide.
widgetGeometry.labelPadsFurtherThanThe2: {label} pads further than the display is tall.
widgetGeometry.labelHasNoSizeThe: {label} has no size; the device needs a width and a height above zero.
widgetGeometry.labelSpendsClaimedPixelsOn: {label} spends {claimed} pixels on its border and inset, which its {width}×{height} box has no room for.
widgetGeometry.labelIsThicknessPixelsThick: {label} is {thickness} pixels thick, which does not fit twice across its {width}×{height} box. Give it a radius of its own, or make the box bigger.
widgetGeometry.labelIsThicknessPixelsThick2: {label} is {thickness} pixels thick, which is more than its {radius}-pixel radius can carry.

widgetRules.labelIsASlotWith: {label} is a slot with an appearance; a slot draws nothing, so put a shape behind it.
widgetRules.labelIsASlotAnd: {label} is a slot and also navigates; its tap already means "next page".
widgetRules.labelIsASlotWith2: {label} is a slot with no pages.
widgetRules.labelHasNoPageIn: {label} has no page in the loop, so nothing would bring one back after an event.
widgetRules.whereStaysUpForDuration: {where} stays up for {duration} ms; the device holds one for {mAXIMUM_HOLD_MS}.
widgetRules.whereHasNoTriggerSo: {where} has no trigger, so its telemetry, rules and duration would never be read.
widgetRules.whereHasATriggerBut: {where} has a trigger but watches no telemetry.
widgetRules.whereAppearsOnAChange: {where} appears on a change but for no time at all; give it a duration.
widgetRules.whereAppearsOnAChange2: {where} appears on a change, so its comparison rules would never be read.
widgetRules.whereAppearsOnAComparison: {where} appears on a comparison but has no rule to compare.
widgetRules.ownerNavigatesToAScreen: {owner} navigates to a screen but names none.
widgetRules.ownerNavigatesToScreenScreen: {owner} navigates to screen "{screen}", which this dashboard does not have.
widgetRules.ownerNamesAScreenFor: {owner} names a screen for {type}, which navigates relatively; drop the screen.

widgetValues.whatOfLabelRunsMinimum: {what} of {label} runs {minimum} to {maximum}; the device needs a maximum above the minimum.
widgetValues.labelHasNoSourceSo: {label} has no source, so it would render nothing.
widgetValues.labelNamesTheImageImage: {label} names the image "{image}", which is not an image identifier.
widgetValues.theCaptionOfLabelReads: The caption of {label} reads telemetry but has no text of its own to fall back on.
widgetValues.labelHasLengthStylingRules: {label} has {length} styling rules; the device holds {mAXIMUM_WIDGET_CONDITIONS}.
widgetValues.labelHasAColourRamp: {label} has a colour ramp with one stop; a ramp interpolates between two.
widgetValues.labelHasAColourRamp2: {label} has a colour ramp with {length} stops; the device holds {mAXIMUM_COLOR_STOPS}.
widgetValues.labelHasNoSegmentsSo: {label} has no segments, so nothing would light.
widgetValues.whatOfLabelReadsName: {what} of {label} reads "{name}", which is not a telemetry field.

bridgeService.alreadyRunning: The telemetry link is already running.
bridgeService.portInUse: Port {port} is already taken. Choose another one here and in the plugin.
